summary: The one grammar flag (gebonden) is dismissed as an attributive adjective, and the Dutch is the most natural of the three (verdwijnt achter, fronted b013). But two glossed words in b010 (gebonden, pockets) have plain equivalents in known words, and 'maken kleine stapels' is a calque; the rest of the vocabulary FAIL is tool noise (volstaan, elk, voorste …).

findings.problem: gebonden in the sense 'hardback' is unknown to the reader (binden is known only as 'to tie'), and a plain equivalent of the same meaning exists in known words.
findings.evidence: lexicon: binden A2 'to tie', gebonden not an entry; hard A1, kaft A2; V1/V2 use 'met een harde kaft'
findings.required_fix: 'Sommige planken staan helemaal vol boeken met een harde kaft: wetenschap, wiskunde, geschiedenis en al het andere.' (drop 'met' after vol to avoid met … met; frees one gloss slot).

findings.problem: pocket is unknown to the reader and a false friend, and a plain equivalent of the same meaning exists in known words.
findings.evidence: lexicon status unknown; zacht A1, kaft A2; V2 uses 'met een zachte kaft'
findings.required_fix: 'Op andere planken staan twee rijen sciencefiction met een zachte kaft.' (parallel to 'met een harde kaft' after L1).

findings.problem: 'stapels maken' with books as subject is a calque of 'making little heaps'; Dutch books 'liggen in/op stapels' or 'vormen stapels'.

findings.required_fix: 'De boeken stromen over naar de tafels en de banken en liggen in kleine stapels onder de ramen.'

flag_decisions.reason: Attributive participle used as a plain adjective ('gebonden boeken' = hardback books), not a clause-replacing participle phrase; restricted.md allows adjectival participles. The problem with the word is vocabulary, handled in L1.

tool_feedback.reason: correctly reported at review level: an attributive participle is the reviewer's call; no other construction missed in 13 sentences.
'staan helemaal vol' is staan + predicate adjective; the separable-verb joiner produced the B1 verb volstaan, which is not in the text.
lexicon has elk known A1 (ADJ/PRON); the DET token's candidate 'elk' is also produced by the de-inflection heuristic and then rejected on POS mismatch (ieder passes).
superlative of known A1 voor; here lemmatised as NOUN 'voorste' (in V1/V2 as 'voorst', a place-name entry) — -ste superlatives should de-inflect to the base.
superlative of known A1 achter; no -ste rule in _deinflect.
compound splitter looks up the raw head 'dozen' (not an entry); it needs to de-inflect the head (doos A1) and report the singular lemma.
direct B1 hit pre-empts the compound-of-known-parts rule (boek A1 + kast A1); it then fills the stretch budget and every cluster.
beschaafd is known A2; the on- prefix is not stripped.
head zoon A1, modifier adoptie an international cognate absent from the lexicon.
international loanword; a cognate/loanword list would avoid this.
resolved via the participle rule to binden A2 and so counted as known+glossed, but the sense 'hardback' is not the known sense 'to tie'; sense shifts are invisible to the tool.
after removing the items above the scene has one unglossed B1 token (overstromen) in 160: ~99% known; the FAIL verdict is a tool artefact.
8 per 1000 floors to 1 on a 160-token scene; use a per-scene minimum.
